title: Restructure bundled hlx-cli skill: progressive disclosure + CI sync
description: Tour of the 8 files created/modified to restructure the bundled skill with progressive disclosure, full CLI surface coverage, new reference documents, and CI enforcement.

steps.title: Trigger-heavy YAML description
steps.description: The YAML frontmatter description (481 chars, <= 1024 limit) front-loads trigger keywords for both CLI-ops (HELIX_API_KEY, HELIX_URL, inspect, tickets) and ticket-writing (ticket prompting, install recovery). This enables accurate agent activation regardless of whether the request is about CLI operations or ticket authoring.

steps.title: Progressive-disclosure body: Workflow section
steps.description: The body follows a 10-section progressive-disclosure layout (9 ## headings). Workflow comes first as the highest-frequency agent task. Each section is concise; detailed content lives in linked reference files to stay within the 5,000-token body budget.

steps.title: Ticket work gotchas section
steps.description: Documents operational traps proven in practice: --description vs --description-file file-path detection, 10,000-char cap, dependency flags, --dry-run, update-description, and --mode RESEARCH guidance.

steps.title: Full CLI surface: tickets list flags
steps.description: Expanded from 127 to 387 lines. Every subcommand at every depth, every long-form flag, all enum values. This section shows the previously-missing tickets list flags (--search, --user, --status, --status-not-in, --archived, --sprint, --json).

steps.title: Mode enum values and description-file flag
steps.description: tickets create now documents the full --mode enum (AUTO|BUILD|FIX|RESEARCH|EXECUTE) and the --description-file flag separately from --description, addressing the CLI file-path detection gotcha.

steps.title: Library comments with rating enums
steps.description: The deepest nesting level (depth 3: hlx library comments post) now documents --section, --rating, --reply-to flags and all rating enum values (thumbs-up/up, thumbs-down/down, love).

steps.title: GitHub-release-asset update flow
steps.description: Documents the 7-step staged update pipeline derived from src/update/check.ts, perform.ts, and validate.ts. Covers GitHub API resolution, tarball download, in-process extraction, validation checks, and atomic rename-based swap with .bak rollback.

steps.title: Broken-install recovery
steps.description: Step-by-step recovery: try hlx update first, then manual tarball download from GitHub releases. Includes a diagnostic table mapping symptoms to likely causes and fixes. No npm install/uninstall/link recommendations.

steps.title: Core Rule: hard-constraint language
steps.description: The ticket-authoring guide uses hard constraints (must, must not, do not, fail closed) throughout. The Core Rule section establishes that every ticket is a self-contained contract with explicit scope, failure behavior, and cardinality semantics.

steps.title: Common Failure Modes with examples
steps.description: All 5 failure modes documented with concrete examples: scope expansion, over-optimization, fail-open, batch/cardinality, and domain vocabulary drift (e.g., SDF AccountConfiguration vs Objects).

steps.title: Recursive --help token collection
steps.description: The core algorithm: recursively walk --help output starting from the top-level command. At each level, extract subcommand names, long-form flags, and enum values. Handles pipe-separated alternatives (org current|list|switch), angle-bracket enums, and prose-format rating values.

steps.title: Coverage check and exit codes
steps.description: For each extracted token, check case-sensitive substring match against backtick-stripped SKILL.md + commands.md content. Exit 0 = all covered, exit 1 = missing tokens listed to stderr, exit 2 = script error. The CI workflow fails the PR on any non-zero exit.

steps.title: CI workflow: skill surface sync
steps.description: Triggers on pull_request and push to main. Uses Node 22 (matching build-release.yml), npm ci (triggers tsc build via prepare script), then runs the parser. No secrets needed since --help works without auth via configOrHelp() stub.
